clue.text: Get Edward into the way of doing business

indicators.note: into tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to get something is to procure it
Ed is the short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Someone tells Edward to get himself into the right way of doing business.
explanation.definitionFit: A procedure is an established method or routine for carrying out a task.

clue.text: In fact performing Lear before second half of July

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters of Lear are put through their paces, rearranged
second half of takes the last two of July's four letters

explanation.surface: An actor really is performing King Lear before late July.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' turns LEAR into REAL; the second half of July is LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Really means truly, as a matter of actual truth.

clue.text: One in cloak had savoury

indicators.note: in places one inside the cloak word

parts.note: a cape is a sleeveless cloak
an is the indefinite article meaning one

explanation.surface: Someone in a cloak had a savoury snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small savoury appetiser served on bread or pastry.

clue.text: Scotsman found posh young lady after party

indicators.note: after puts the posh young lady following the party

parts.note: a do is a party
U means upper-class, posh
gal is a casual word for a girl or young lady

explanation.surface: A Scot met a posh young woman after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class usage, so it means posh.
explanation.definitionFit: Dougal is a traditional Scottish man's name.

clue.text: Turnover that's sweet?

parts.note: a turnover is a pastry, and this dessert is rolled over on itself, a sweet rolled-up pudding

explanation.surface: A question about a sugary pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: The roly-poly is a British suet pudding spread with jam and rolled up; 'roly-poly' suggests rolling over.
explanation.definitionFit: This rolled jam-and-suet dessert is a sweet course that has literally been turned over on itself.

clue.text: Head first

explanation.surface: Two terse words.
explanation.definitionFit: A principal is the head of a school or college; as an adjective it means first or main.

clue.text: Bachelor on verge of powerful attack

indicators.note: on puts the bachelor above the verge in this down clue

parts.note: a verge is the grassy roadside

explanation.surface: A bachelor on the brink of a mighty assault.
explanation.walkthrough: The verge is the British word for the grass strip at the side of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside is the firing of all a ship's guns on one side, hence any fierce verbal attack.

clue.text: Shout after something has been stolen

definitions.text: Shout after something has been stolen

parts.words: Shout after something has been stolen
parts.note: the cry raised at a robbery to alert others to catch the culprit

explanation.surface: A cry raised after a theft.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the traditional cry to raise the alarm and get bystanders to catch a robber.

clue.text: A skirt model put on mount

parts.note: a ra-ra skirt is a short layered flared skirt, so ra-ra stands for skirt
the Model T was Henry Ford's famous car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: A model is told to put on a skirt before stepping up onto a mount.
explanation.walkthrough: A RA-RA skirt is a short frilly skirt popular in the 1980s; the Model T Ford supplies the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Ararat in Turkey is the mountain where Noah's Ark traditionally came to rest.

clue.text: A drink outside completely finished in a lucrative way

indicators.note: outside means the drink's letters go around the A

parts.note: gin is a spirit, a drink
something fully done is completely finished

explanation.surface: Someone finishes a drink outside, profitably.
explanation.definitionFit: Gainfully means profitably, in a way that brings in money.

clue.text: Pitch tent, irritating mean police constable

indicators.note: irritating suggests the letters of mean are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A camper is irritated by a mean police officer while pitching a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: To encamp is to set up camp, which means putting up tents.

clue.text: Contented after rebuke, being punch-drunk

indicators.note: after places the word for contented following the word for rebuke

parts.note: a slap is a sharp reproof or rebuke
contented means happy

explanation.surface: Someone feels contented after a telling-off, as if dazed by a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaphappy describes someone dazed or giddy as if from repeated blows, like a punch-drunk boxer.

clue.text: Chief equipment's initially trash

parts.note: kit means equipment, and the 's adds an S
Ch. is an abbreviation for chief, used here as its initials

explanation.surface: The boss's gear turns out to be rubbish from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' signals that Chief is cut to its abbreviation CH; it joins after KITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch is tasteless, cheap art or decoration, the kind of thing dismissed as rubbish.

clue.text: Music that cannot be done without

definitions.text: Music that cannot be done without

parts.words: Music that cannot be done without
parts.note: a musical part marked as essential and not to be omitted

explanation.surface: Some music is indispensable.
explanation.definitionFit: Obbligato, Italian for obligatory, marks an instrumental part that must be played and cannot be left out.

clue.text: Cooks joint in vessel

parts.note: to steam food is to cook it
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: Someone cooks a joint of meat on board ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamship is a ship driven by steam engines.

clue.text: Rebuild rundown area, produce another photograph of it?

explanation.surface: A plan to rebuild a run-down area and photograph it anew.
explanation.definitionFit: To redevelop is to renovate an area; whimsically, it is also to develop a film again, producing a fresh print.

clue.text: Old measure of length in yellow

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the word yellow

explanation.surface: An old unit of length turns up in a colour word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ell was an old unit of cloth length, about 45 inches in England.

clue.text: Measure a lady

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of measure
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gentleman is told to size up a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Ena is a woman's name, so a particular lady.

clue.text: Fate of Abraham's nephew

explanation.surface: The destiny of Abraham's relative.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot is one's fate in life; in Genesis, Lot was the nephew of Abraham.

clue.text: Involving the first two people in confidence

explanation.surface: A remark about two people sharing a secret.
explanation.walkthrough: In grammar the first person is 'me' and the second is 'you', so a phrase involving both is the answer read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both the speaker and listener (grammatical first and second persons), and is also the idiom for saying something privately.

clue.text: A little exercise that's suitable

parts.note: PT, physical training, is exercise in abbreviated (little) form

explanation.surface: A small amount of exercise is just right.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means fitting or appropriate.

clue.text: Crusty drone?

parts.note: playfully read as something like a loaf with a crust, but really an idle person who does no work

explanation.surface: A grumpy, idle old person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crusty' suggests bread, a loaf; a drone is an idler who lazes about.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler who lounges about doing nothing is described by the word, as a drone bee does no work.

clue.text: Start of sentimentality in marriage harmony

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the word for marriage

parts.note: a marriage is a union

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of sentimentality

explanation.surface: A bit of sentimentality in a marriage makes for harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing in unison means together on one note, in accord.

clue.text: Tailor-made bridge

indicators.note: made suggests the letters are formed into a new shape

explanation.surface: A bespoke bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailor-made' hides the anagram indicator in its second half.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the famous bridge over Venice's Grand Canal.

clue.text: Antiseptic pioneer knocked top off bubble on skin

indicators.note: knocked top off removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: a blister is a fluid-filled bubble on the skin

explanation.surface: A medical pioneer knocks the top off a skin blister.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery in the 1860s.

clue.text: I repeatedly knitted another picture!

indicators.note: another signals a different arrangement of the letters
repeatedly tells us the letter I is used twice

explanation.surface: Someone proudly announces they have knitted yet another picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An Identikit is a composite picture of a suspect's face built from witness descriptions.

clue.text: Talk he had cut

parts.note: to gas is to talk idly at length
he'd is the contraction of he had

explanation.surface: Gossip that a man had a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Gashed means slashed, having made a deep wound.

clue.text: Solid suet remarkably loose

indicators.note: remarkably suggests the letters are behaving unusually, rearranged

explanation.surface: Solid suet turns out remarkably loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissolute describes someone loose in morals, given to indulgence.

clue.text: Fox to tear into stand

indicators.note: into places one word inside the other

parts.note: tod is an old dialect word for a fox
to rip is to tear

explanation.surface: A fox tears into a stand.
explanation.walkthrough: TOD is an old word for a fox, mostly met in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripod is a three-legged stand for a camera or instrument.

clue.text: Caught, we hear, behind a trap in battle

indicators.note: behind places the sounded word after the others

parts.note: taken as written
a gin is a snare or trap for animals

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: caught sounds like court in non-rhotic British speech

explanation.surface: Someone is caught behind a trap during a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech 'caught' and 'court' sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Agincourt was the 1415 battle where Henry V's English army defeated the French.
